cases.scope: Finite differential contract for phased binding identity, ordered initialization, late demand, opaque observation, artifact epoch validation, path change ordering and two-worker load claims, including overlap between split initialization, opaque fallback and path publication. Claim settlement assumes a fair enabled completion or failure transition. The deferred evaluator implementation and native performance require separate replay evidence. A deferred phase visit keeps its admitted image across a controlled search-path change. A split initializer may run from a resident phase only when its body witness matches. The fixture specifies exact initial runtime image sets independently of the candidate closure. Retaining an unused branch or introducing an extra proxy image violates this footprint contract even when semantic safety holds. The expected mode is derived from admitted proof and phase evidence, so unnecessary whole-graph fallback also violates the contract.

Finite characterization of three ordered checkpoints and four logical members. Distinct members can share a physical image across scopes. Publication preserves order, respects preexisting residency, checks artifact replacement at open, and rejects ambiguous native linker names. Each checkpoint's charge is exactly the newly mapped image set relative to the process baseline and every earlier checkpoint. Resetting residency on entering a different scope or charging an import image again are rejected counterexamples.

Finite characterization of deferring a native provider whose same-path content can change before or after admission. A matching provider in a retained sealed generation can be deferred. Mutable inputs keep ordinary import failure order. The state model assumes sealed contents are immutable until the last deferred demand.
